words.gloss: is it because of the saying?

literal: To those who are ruined, friends do not exist, is it because of that saying, O heart, you, as desired, after him go?
translation: O my heart! Is it because of the saying that those who are ruined have no friends, that you follow him as you please, leaving me behind?
modern: நெஞ்சே! கெட்டவர்களுக்கு நண்பர்கள் இல்லை என்ற பழமொழி உண்மையோ? நீ உன் விருப்பப்படி என்னை விட்டுவிட்டு அவரிடமே செல்கிறாயே.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine addresses her own heart, which is eager to return to her lover despite his neglect. She asks if her heart is abandoning her because of the common proverb that 'those who are ruined have no friends' (கெட்டார்க்கு நட்டார் இல்). Here, 'கெட்டார்' (the ruined) refers to the heroine herself, who is wasted by the pain of separation. Her heart, which should act as her loyal friend ('நட்டார்'), is instead deserting her to go ('செலல்') after her lover according to its own desire ('பெட்டாங்கு'). This playful accusation highlights her helplessness and the conflict between her dignity and her desire.
